item.title: Subtitle Launches Godzilla-Inspired Capsule Featuring Laser-Burned Denim Jackets
item.description:
Summary

Subtitle's "TIDES" is an eight-piece collection centering on Godzilla’s ties to the sea.Garment-washed denim and heat ray-inspired laser burning define the lineup.Highlights include a Type I jacket, a noragi-style jacket and a 1:1954 scale hat.

Following its successful debut collection centered on Jujutsu Kaisen, Subtitle has teamed up with TOHO International on "TIDES" -- an eight-piece collection that draws on more than 70 years of Godzilla history. The range draws its aesthetic influence and inspiration from Godzilla’s lifelong tie to the ocean, ranging from the folklore of Odo Island to its first appearance in the original 1954 film. “We treated all of it as source material: the sea became washed denim, and the heat ray became an artwork technique,” Subtitle founder and creative director Liang Shi said in an official statementThat idea shapes how the garments are made. Denim is the backbone of the collection because, like the ocean Godzilla rises from, water changes it and garment washing across the lineup nods to the monster’s emergence from the sea. The heat ray inspired a second technique: lasers burn artwork directly into the fabric, permanently changing its color and texture rather than printing on top. Both come together in the Godzilla Minus Zero Black Type I Denim Jacket. It references the new Godzilla Minus Zero film’s 1940s setting through the Type I, a workwear jacket in production during that era. Rebuilt in 14 oz black denim with double front pleats, the jacket is fitted with a single chest pocket, an adjustable back belt, mixed antique silver and copper hardware and a large laser-burned Godzilla across the back.The Godzilla Blue Denim Jacket borrows the collarless shape of the noragi, a traditional Japanese work jacket worn by farmers, fishermen and craftspeople. Its back carries laser-printed, ukiyo-e-inspired artwork by Matt Frank, originally created as the subscription variant cover for Godzilla: Rage Across Time #1. The Light Blue Washed Denim Overshirt evokes the sea more directly: unstitched seams at the hem, cuffs and chest pocket reveal deeper blue denim beneath pale laser-printed artwork, suggesting waves and whitecaps.The rest of the lineup moves from the screen to the shoreline. A reversible liner jacket pairs a quilted nylon patchwork bandana print, hiding Godzilla motifs and finished with onion-quilt stitching, with a black denim reverse. The French terry Bandana Hoodie is modeled on vintage fisherman’s smocks, a nod to the fishing communities at the heart of Godzilla’s origin story. The faded Odo Island Souvenir T-Shirt plays on the classic tourist tee, and barrel-leg Paisley Pants hide Godzilla and footprint motifs in a print that is dyed after printing for a tonal finish. The most playful piece is the 1:1954 Scale Denim Hat. It shrinks the original 50-meter Godzilla down at a ratio matching its debut year, producing a 2.56 cm embroidered figure on the front, with “King of the Monsters” stitched across the back.Check out the campaign for the collection in the gallery above. Subtitles' "TIDES" collection is now available to shop exclusively on Godzilla.com. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Subtitle (@subtitle.club)

item.title: The Etsy Design Awards Are Back With a Spotlight on Next-Gen Makers
item.description:
After championing creativity for the last seven years, the Etsy Design Awards are back for 2026, bringing a fresh focus on emerging creators and cutting-edge artistic makers across its seller community.With a new generation of buyers seeking unique, one-of-a-kind pieces for their homes and wardrobes, this year’s awards celebrate the rising popularity of handicraft trends, giving shoppers a front-row look into what true handmade craftsmanship looks like today.Alongside the flagship “Grand Prize” and “People’s Pick” categories, there are 13 new awards designed around the playful flair of the creators. From “Future Heirloom” and “Worth Every Stitch” to more abstract themes such as “Touch Grass” and “Conversation Starter,” the new additions aim to break the mold of conventional competition structures with a personalized touch.Thousands of entries were whittled down to 150 finalists and 15 winners, judged by a panel including Etsy’s Trend Expert Dayna Isom Johnson and founder of fashion and lifestyle label Lisa Says Gah, Lisa Bühler. The label serves as the inaugural brand partner of the Etsy Design Awards, with Bühler applying her expertise in identifying new style trends to the submissions to explore how they’re creating cultural buzz beyond the awards.Having now announced the winners, it’s clear there’s a new creative class coming to the forefront, who create a world of items that embrace individuality and artistic expression. Some of our favourite winners are “Rising Star” Sitoë Thiam, who creates vibrant knotted macramé that doubles up as bag chains, and Cait Mellor’s delicate crochet, which won the “Touch Grass” award. And not forgetting the Grand Prize Winner, Texan ceramicist Jacqueline Sanchez, who took the crown with her scaled vase.While only one winner has been chosen for each category, the Etsy Design Awards aim to recognize those challenging traditional art forms and help the next generation of talented makers get discovered.Head to Hypebeast’s Instagram channels this week as we delve deeper into some of the Etsy seller stories or visit Etsy’s dedicated webpage for more information.

item.title: Zenith Heads West for Its Second G.F.J. Double Signed Collaboration
item.description:
Summary

Zenith taps J.N. Shapiro for the second G.F.J. Calibre 135 Double Signed edition.A California-made guilloché dial features barleycorn, basketweave and Infinity Weave patterns/Damaskeened bridges bring American flair to the Swiss movement.

Zenith is continuing its Double Signed program, a series that revives the golden-era tradition of watches bearing two makers' names. After the first edition with Tokyo's Naoya Hida & Co., the Le Locle Manufacture has teamed up with American independent J.N. Shapiro for the second edition.Both releases are built on the G.F.J., named after Zenith founder Georges Favre-Jacot and designed as the modern home of the Calibre 135, the most decorated observatory chronometer movement in history. Joshua Shapiro started his brand in a home workshop in 2018 making guilloché dials, and it has since grown to produce its own Caliber 26 movement and the Resurgence watch. "The Calibre 135 is one of the holy grails of watchmaking. To get to beautify such a functionally historic calibre has been really exciting," Shapiro said in the release.The dial of the Zenith G.F.J. Calibre 135 Double Signed With J.N. Shapiro was made entirely at Shapiro's California workshop. Its silver base carries three hand-cut guilloché patterns, made on rose-engine and straight-line machines: barleycorn around the outer ring, basketweave in the center, and Shapiro's signature Infinity Weave on the small seconds subdial. Applied 18k rose gold rings, hour markers and nameplates frame the textures, including a "Zenith | J.N. Shapiro" double signature and the G.F.J. initials.Unlike the Naoya Hida edition, which focused on the dial and hands, this collaboration extends to the movement. The bridges of the hand-wound Calibre 135 are decorated with damaskeening, a mix of Côtes de Genève stripes and guilloché patterns closely associated with antique American pocket watches, bringing an American touch to a Swiss movement.Beneath the decoration, the re-engineered Calibre 135 runs at 2.5 Hz with a large variable-inertia balance, a Breguet overcoil and Charles Fleck's double arrow-shaped regulator. It offers 72 hours of power reserve and a stop-seconds function, and it is COSC-certified to within ±2 seconds a day. It sits in a 39mm rose gold case, 10.5mm thick and water-resistant to 50 meters, with a sapphire caseback that shows off the damaskeened movement. The watch comes with three straps, brown Cordovan, beige nubuck alligator and black calf, plus an 18k rose gold pin buckle engraved with the G.F.J. initials, and a matching rose gold bracelet is available on request.Limited to 25 examples, the G.F.J. Calibre 135 Double Signed with J.N. Shapiro timepiece is priced at 68,900 CHF (approx. $ 82,824 USD). For more information, head over to Zenith's official website.
